abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become integrated into human-subjects research, understanding how participants perceive and consent to data use is central to building transparent and trustworthy research practices. We conducted a scenario-based study in which 157 participants evaluated 12 scenarios (sampled from a pool of 864), each varying across seven parameters: topic sensitivity, LLM management, data anonymization, data retention, model training, additional data access, and additional consent. We find that the effects of parameters on participants’ willingness to participate were mediated by their attitudinal evaluations—most robustly comfort, usefulness and safety—with no residual direct effects (consistent with full mediation). Anonymization and additional consent increased participation willingness, while indefinite data retention reduced it. Surprisingly, corporate LLM management (vs. federal) did not reduce participation, and data use for model training or personalization—despite potential data leakage—tended to increase participation willingness. We conclude with design implications for consent processes, transparency mechanisms, and governance practices that align research with participants’ stated preferences.

ur.ai_reason: LLM场景实验测量参与者知情与参与意愿
ur.tldr: 通过157名参与者评估12种人机对话研究场景，考察数据匿名化、留存、训练、访问及同意机制对参与意愿的影响。舒适度、实用性与安全感完全中介参与意愿；匿名化和追加同意提高意愿，无限期留存降低意愿。

title: Understanding people’s willingness to participate in human-LLM conversational interaction research studies - a scenario study
title_zh: 了解人们参与人类-LLM对话交互研究的意愿：一项情景研究
